title: Contrasting Effects of Flufenamic Acid and Nabumetone on Photosynthetic Apparatus Reveal Distinct Modes of NSAID Phytotoxicity
content: Pharmaceutical contaminants are an increasing environmental concern, yet the mechanisms by which non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) affect photosynthetic organisms remain poorly understood. We investigated the direct effects of flufenamic acid (FFA) and nabumetone (NBT) on isolated chloroplasts and thylakoid membranes of spinach (Spinacia oleracea L.) using oxygen evolution and uptake measurements, chlorophyll a fluorescence in vivo analysis (OJIP test), and transmission electron microscopy. FFA induced a strong concentration-dependent inhibition of photosynthetic activity, causing complete suppression of chloroplast oxygen evolution at concentrations ≥1000 μM. This effect was accompanied by impaired PSII photochemistry, restricted electron transport, enhanced energy dissipation, and severe disruption of chloroplast ultra-structure. The responses were considerably stronger in isolated thylakoids than in intact chloroplasts, indicating that photosynthetic membranes constitute the primary target of FFA toxicity. In contrast, NBT produced only minor changes in PSII-related chlorophyll a fluorescence in vivo parameters and chloroplast structure despite reducing oxygen evolution. NBT stimulated oxygen uptake and increased PSI-related parameters in isolated thylakoids, suggesting enhanced electron transport toward PSI acceptors and a possible uncoupling-like effect. Our results demonstrate that structurally distinct NSAIDs may affect photosynthesis through different membrane-related mechanisms, highlighting the importance of compound-specific evaluation when assessing the ecological risks of pharmaceutical contaminants.
